title: A Target-Aware Analysis of Data Augmentation for Hate Speech Detection
benchmark_measurement: Performance of hate speech detection models on posts targeting religious groups, specifically measuring improvements in hate-F1 scores for the 'religion' category and for posts targeting 'Muslims'.
findings: The baseline model performed poorly on detecting hate speech targeting religion (48.5% F1-score). Data augmentation significantly improved performance, with a combination of traditional (EDA) and generative (T5 model) methods yielding the best results, increasing the F1-score for the religion category to 62.8%. Analysis using the HateCheck test suite for the 'Muslims' target confirmed that augmentation provides substantial performance gains, improving the F1-score from a baseline of 14.7% to over 60% in the best-performing augmented model.
